page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals average single-core performance but weaker multi-core and memory capabilities. The single-core Geekbench score of 1742.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1607.88 fall into the average tier. However, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2210.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1899.38. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 152.03 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 12.74 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and key-value operations show lower relative performance, with Redis SET operations executing at 2.43 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 1019.5.

This instance represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient option within the Intel-based Gen7 family, trading off high-throughput multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth for lower baseline costs. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for specialized vector and matrix math. Given the single-core efficiency and limited multi-core scaling, the instance is appropriate for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments.
